A: State the required permission on a line `Auth: <scope>`.
Say whether repeating the call is safe on a line `Idempotent: yes` or `Idempotent: no`.
Show one example call on a line that starts with `$ curl `.
The first line must be a level-3 Markdown heading with the method and path in backticks, for example ### `GET /v1/invoices/{id}`.
Keep the whole entry to at most 90 words.
State the API version that introduced the endpoint on a line `Since: v<version>`, for example `Since: v1.4`.
B: The first line must be the method and path alone in plain text with no Markdown, for example `GET /v1/invoices/{id}`.
Mark the maturity on a line `Stability: stable`, `Stability: beta` or `Stability: deprecated`.
Name the media type of the response on a line such as `Content-Type: application/json`.
List the parameters in a Markdown table whose header row is `| Name | In | Type | Description |`.
Include an example request written as a shell line beginning with `$ curl `.
Document the response statuses under a line `Responses:` with at least three bullets of the form `- <status code>: <meaning>`.

relations.reason: A4 requires the first line to be a level-3 Markdown heading with backticks around the method and path, while B1 requires the first line to be plain text with no Markdown. These cannot both be satisfied for the same first line.
Both A3 and B5 require including a curl example call starting with '$ curl '. The content and format are effectively identical, so they ask for the same thing.

A5 limits the entire entry to at most 90 words, while B4 requires a Markdown table of parameters which can be verbose. Including the table may easily exceed the word limit, so both rules can only be satisfied if the rest of the content is highly concise and the table is minimized.
